text.p: UPM-Kymmene Oy, Europe's largest forestry group, on Tuesday reported a slightly sharper than expected slide in earnings for 1996 but said it expected a steady performance this year.

With profit before extraordinary items down 43 percent to 3.56 billion markka ($700.1 million) from a record 6.28 billion in the bumper year 1995, UPM-Kymmene held the value of its dividend at 4.50 markka, much of it in stock in a subsidiary.
The payout would comprise 1.50 markka in cash and 3.00 markka in shares in engineering group Rauma Oy, in which UPM owns a stake of 73.3 percent, UPM-Kymmene said in a statement.

If the payout is approved, this would reduce UPM-Kymmene's stake in Rauma to 59.9 percent, the company said, adding that "In the future it is intended to reduce this to below 50 percent through other means."
Rauma, reporting simultaneously with its parent company, said its profit nudged up to 679 million markka from 671 million in 1995 and it too forecast a steady 1996 showing.
UPM-Kymmene's result was slightly below the median of analysts' forecasts which had been for a 1996 profit of 3.70 billion markka in a 2.65 to 4.44 billion range.
"At present UPM-Kymmene expects the financial result for 1997 to be similar to that for last year," the company said.
Economic growth was expected to increase gradually in Europe, the company's main market, and this would increase paper consumption, UPM said.

"Deliveries of printing and writing papers are expected to be up on 1996, although sales prices will be lower, at least in the early part of the year," it said. Printing paper prices have probably bottomed out, it added.

"Better demand early in 1997 has raised capacity utilisation rates and paved the way for an increase in sales prices," UPM said. "It is hoped to raise fine paper and LWC prices during the first quarter of the year," it added.
Its net 1996 sales fell to 51.75 billion markka from 54.74 billion, with operating profit down less sharply than profit after extras to 5.59 billion markka from 8.50 billion.
